Ămăthūs, untis, f., = Ἀμαθοῦς (acc. Gr. Amathunta, ),
a town in the southern part of Cyprus, consisting of two ports, one on the coast, now Old Limasol, and the other on a hill inland, now Agios Tychanos, ; ; sacred to Venus, who is hence called ămăthūsĭa, ; ; .—Hence, ămăthūsĭă-cus, a, um, of Amathus: bidentes, Merk. la:noun:Amazon.html:
Ămāzon, ŏnis, f., = Ἀμαζών, plur. Amazones [a Scythian word of dub. signif.; acc. to an etymological fancy, as if from ἀ-μαζός, without breast; , relates that their right breast was removed in childhood, to enable them to handle the bow more conveniently],
an Amazon; and plur., Amazons, warlike women, who dwelt on the river Thermodon.
Lit.: Threiciae Amazones,: exsultat Amazon,: Amazon Mavortia,: peltata,—
Metaph., a heroine of love, ; .—Hence,
ămāzŏnĭ-cus, a, um, Amazonian, Mel.1, 19, 13; ; .—
ămāzŏ-nis, ĭdis, f., = Amazon, an Amazon: Amazonidum agmina,: Amazonidum gens,: Amazonidum turba,.—Also, title of a poem composed by a poet named Marsus, .—
ămāzŏnĭus, a, um, poet. for Amazonicus, Amazonian: securis,, and : genus,: vir Amazonius, i. e. Hippolytus, the son of an Amazon by Theseus, .
